title: Accuracy- and Real-Time-Aware 4D Radar Preprocessing for Autonomous Driving Perception Systems

problem.summary: However, deploying 4D radar in embedded environments with limited hardware resources requires radar-representation preprocessing that jointly considers perception accuracy, real-time performance, and computational complexity.

background.summary: First, Percentile-based 3D Shape Preservation (P3DP) extracts point clouds from radar tensors while preserving object-shape information and suppressing noise and false alarms.

evidence.quote: First, Percentile-based 3D Shape Preservation (P3DP) extracts point clouds from radar tensors while preserving object-shape information and suppressing noise and false alarms.
Second, Multi-frame-based Noise Point Discrimination using Kernel Density Estimation (MF-KDE) improves the density and reliability of sparse radar point clouds.

solution.summary: I NTRODUCTION 4D radar measures the three-dimensional position of an object by providing elevation information in addition to the range, azimuth, and Doppler information available from conventional automotive radar.
solution.approach: I NTRODUCTION 4D radar measures the three-dimensional position of an object by providing elevation information in addition to the range, azimuth, and Doppler information available from conventional automotive radar.
components: Because 4D radar uses electromagnetic waves with longer wavelengths than those used by cameras or LiDAR, it provides relatively stable measurements under adverse weather conditions such as rain, fog, and snow [1]-[3].
It can also directly estimate object velocity through the Doppler effect.
These properties have made 4D radar a promising next-generation sensor for improving the robustness of autonomous driving perception systems [2].
